text:
ashok: thinking out loud — we need to decide whether SLA negotiation (the "broker" that translates tenant SLOs into headroom/reservation budgets) should live in the control plane or as a sidecar in the pool operator.
marie: +1 to explicitly discussing ownership. control-plane broker gives global visibility for fairness and cost but couples control-plane latency to scale decisions.
jordan: control-plane makes sense for cross-tenant fairness, but if control-plane is down we risk not renewing bursts -> outages. what do we do for degraded mode?
lia: propose split: control-plane computes policy & global quotas, operator keeps a local short-lived lease for burst admission (30s) so decisions can continue if CP unreachable.
as hok: @lia leaning that way. need explicit semantics for lease TTL, renewal, and metrics for staleness. also how preemption signals flow.
tim: small API sketch:
```
POST /broker/evaluate
body: { tenant_id, requested_tokens, latency_target }
resp: { decision: allow|queue|deny, lease_ms: 30000, reason }
```
marie: ensure response includes `variant_hint` to pick a cheaper/quantized model if full capacity denied.
sasha: important trade: local operator admitting without CP consent increases risk of headroom oversubscription. maybe require signed token from CP that encodes remaining budget.
ashok: signed token + short TTL seems safe. operator verifies signature and decrements encoded credits. CP can revoke by rotating signing key but revocation lag exists.
jordan: we should add fallback policies in operator: if token invalid, allow zero-latency prewarm if below X% utilization, else deny. keep a small emergency headroom for health checks.
lia: rollout plan idea: 1) implement read-only broker API on CP, operator consumes tokens optionally; 2) enable signed-token mode behind feature flag for selected tenants; 3) run e2e load with chaos (cp partitions) to see failover behavior.
tim: metrics to capture: token-issuance-rate, token-consumption-rate, operator-stale-decision-rate, headroom-oversubscription-incidents, decision-latency. put everything in pool-level dashboard.
sasha: also add cost accounting: when operator admits using token, emit cost attribution event so billing reflects burst consumption.
orch-bot: deploy - canary started for broker v1 on staging, 5 pools targeted.
marie: compatibility note: existing autoscaler currently expects a single numeric headroom. broker needs to expose both conservative_headroom and soft_headroom to preserve behavior.
ashok: question for API folks — should `soft_headroom` be a percentage or absolute GPU slots? pros/cons?
jordan: percentage is workload-agnostic but harder to reason about small pools. absolute slots are precise but need CP to know pool size. maybe accept both and normalize server-side.
lia: eviction semantics: when soft_headroom exhausted, prefer model-variant degrade or preemptible evictions before killing running requests. document clear order of operations.
tim: small config schema proposal:
```
broker_policy: {
  global_quota: <tokens>,
  per_pool: { min_slots, soft_headroom_pct, lease_ms }
}
```
marie: agree — let's add a `grace_preheat_ms` to account for prewarm latency for cold models.
sasha: we need a test harness to simulate tenant bursts + CP partition + clock skew. recommend using our chaos infra + a synthetic-workload generator.
ashok: OK next steps: marie & tim to draft API + config proto by EOD Wed, lia & jordan to prototype operator-side lease handling and signed token verification, sasha to wire billing events. we'll loop back Thurs sync.
marie: I pushed a short doc to the design board: https://redwood-internal/designs/sla-broker-split (notes + sequence diagrams). feedback welcome. :mag: 
jordan: quick nit — call the token field `burst_credits` not `tokens` to avoid confusion with auth tokens.
lia: noted. also add emergency-mode flag that forces operator to only admit health-checks if CP unreachable.
as hok: thanks all. this should avoid coupling scale-critical decisions to CP availability while preserving global cost/fairness. can we add one pager for SRE on how to run degraded-mode drills?
sasha: will start a checklist.
orch-bot: deploy - canary completed on staging, metrics look steady. :white_check_mark:
